translations.answer: Project contributors note that the floating base is not included in the standard URDF. Directly calling buildModel(filename, model) will fix the base to the universe, and q does not contain base position/orientation. When a humanoid has a floating base, a JointModelFreeFlyer root_joint should be constructed and a buildModel with root_joint called to override. The original author modified this and obtained TALOS model.nq=39, model.nv=38; compared to fixed base, 32/32, the configuration increased by 7 and speed increased by 6.
translations.applicability: Applies to the original Pinocchio URDF parser and humanoid with 6-DoF floating base; fixed base tasks should not include the root joint.
translations.credibility.rationale: Environmental, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: Author changed joint type from continuous to revolute and rechecked nq/nv.
translations.details.attempts.1: Author followed the recommendation and called buildModel with JointModelFreeFlyer root_joint to re-import TALOS.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Check spherical, FreeFlyer, and continuous joint parameterizations; do not directly use nq as physical degrees of freedom.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Check if buildModel explicitly passes JointModelFreeFlyer root_joint.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Use randomConfiguration, integrate, and difference/differentiate for configuration, integration, and differentiation, without direct q += v or q1 - q0.
translations.details.effective_fixes.1: Explicitly call buildModel with JointModelFreeFlyer root_joint when a floating base is present.
translations.details.environments.0: 2019 Pinocchio C++/Python; HRP2, ATLAS, TALOS URDF; specific software versions not mentioned.
translations.details.limits.0: continuous and revolute have different angle boundary semantics; do not blindly replace them just to match dimensions in the model.
translations.details.limits.1: q[0:3] and q[3:7] base translation/quaternion arrangements are only applicable to models with explicitly added FreeFlyer.
translations.details.limits.2: Threaded based on 2019 interface; function names and overloads should be verified separately.
translations.details.outcomes.0: Author reported HRP2's nq/nv match expectations after changing joint type from continuous to revolute.
translations.details.outcomes.1: Author added FreeFlyer and obtained TALOS model.nq=39, model.nv=38, matching the maintainer's expectation.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why does Pinocchio's model.nq differ from model.nv, and why does HRP2 show nq=60, nv=30?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: Why does a model built directly from a humanoid URDF lack base position/orientation degrees of freedom?
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Quaternions are represented with 4 configuration components for 3 angular velocity dimensions, and continuous joints also use different manifold parameterizations for nq and nv.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: URDFs do not include floating base joints; direct buildModel fixes the base to the universe.
translations.details.symptoms.0: After importing HRP2, model.nq=60, model.nv=30; configuration dimension seems double the speed dimension.
translations.details.symptoms.1: TALOS direct buildModel results in model.nq=model.nv=32, without expected 7/6 base degrees of freedom.
